issues.legal_issue: A testamentary instrument effects a severance in a joint family only when it clearly and unequivocally expresses an intention to separate.
material_facts: The properties were found to be joint family properties of the deceased and his brother.
The will asserted that there was no ancestral property, referred to property as joint, and directed that the remaining property be kept joint until the deceased’s son attained majority.
The will did not expressly state an intention to end the coparcenary.
issues.conclusion: The will did not effect a severance in the status of the joint family.
issues.legal_principle: Under A. Raghavamma v. A. Chenchamma, a member of a joint Hindu family may bring about separation in status by a definite and unequivocal declaration of an intention to separate, even in a will; the expression of that intention must be brought home to the persons affected. The terms of this will did not establish such an intention.

rule.if: partition_dispute_over_joint_family_property and will_claimed_as_separation and (will_lacked_unequivocal_separation_declaration or will_asserted_property_was_not_joint or will_directed_property_to_remain_joint)

predicates.partition_dispute_over_joint_family_prop: A party sought partition of property that the court found belonged to a joint family.
predicates.will_claimed_as_separation: A party relied on a deceased family member’s will as having separated the family in status.
predicates.will_lacked_unequivocal_separation_decla: The will did not clearly and unambiguously state that its maker intended to separate from the family.
predicates.will_asserted_property_was_not_joint: The will asserted that the property was not joint family property.
predicates.will_directed_property_to_remain_joint: The will directed that property remain joint for a period or until a stated event.

issues.definition: When a party relies on a will to establish separation in a dispute over joint family property, an instrument lacking a clear declaration of separation, or asserting the property was not joint or directing it to remain joint, does not establish separation in status.

issues.legal_issue: A family arrangement is enforceable only when there was an occasion for making it and it was acted upon.
material_facts: The appellant argued that the will should be treated as a family arrangement made by the family manager and assented to on the widow’s behalf.
There was no evidence establishing an occasion for making the alleged arrangement or that it was acted upon.
A letter relied on to support the arrangement was not found genuine, and there was no satisfactory evidence that the widow enjoyed the properties allegedly allotted to her.
issues.conclusion: The alleged family arrangement could not be enforced.
issues.legal_principle: A family arrangement made for the general benefit of the family may be enforced, but the party seeking enforcement must establish that there was an occasion for making the arrangement and that it was acted upon.

rule.if: partition_dispute and family_arrangement_claimed_from_will and (no_occasion_for_arrangement_proved or arrangement_not_shown_to_be_acted_upon)

predicates.partition_dispute: A party sought partition of family property.
predicates.family_arrangement_claimed_from_will: A party claimed that provisions in a will constituted a family arrangement.
predicates.no_occasion_for_arrangement_proved: The party seeking enforcement did not establish an occasion for making the alleged arrangement.
predicates.arrangement_not_shown_to_be_acted_upon: The party seeking enforcement did not establish that the alleged arrangement was acted upon.

issues.definition: In a partition dispute, a family arrangement claimed from a will is not enforceable when the party seeking enforcement fails to establish either an occasion for it or that it was acted upon.

issues.legal_issue: A widow’s share in joint family property under the statutory right to claim partition is determined when she claims partition, not when her husband dies.
material_facts: The widow’s husband died while the properties were found to be joint family property held with his brother.
The widow had no issue with her husband; his son from an earlier marriage died after him and before the partition suit.
The widow later sought partition and claimed the share her husband would have had in the property.
issues.conclusion: The widow was entitled to the share her husband would have been entitled to had he lived on the date she claimed partition; her interest was not fixed by the family’s composition at the date of his death.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(2) of the Hindu Women’s Rights to Property Act, 1937, gives the widow the same interest as her husband had, and section 3(3) gives her the right to claim partition. The court treated this as a statutory interest under which the widow, as her husband’s surviving half, is entitled to the share he would have received if alive when she claimed partition. The interest may fluctuate with changes in family membership and property before partition. The court followed the approach reflected in Chinniah Chettiar v. Sivagami Achi and the decisions cited in support of a fluctuating interest, and disapproved the contrary approach in Jadaobai v. Puranmal and Natarajan Chettiar v. Perumal Ammal. It also noted that the widow’s interest had later been enlarged by section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

predicates.widow_claims_partition_of_joint_family_p: A widow seeks partition of property held by the joint family to which her deceased husband belonged.
predicates.deceased_coparcener_left_widow: A member of the joint family died leaving a widow.
predicates.widow_entitlement_arises_under_statutory: The widow’s asserted entitlement to the property arises from a statutory right associated with her deceased husband’s interest.

issues.definition: When a widow claims partition of joint family property under a statutory right based on her deceased husband’s interest, her share is assessed when she claims partition.
